title: Anti-Money Laundering and Other Matters Bill
what_it_is: Anti-Money Laundering and Other Matters Bill

sections.label: Responsive approach to new risks
sections.summary: The regime is well established internationally, and the approach is to stay responsive and get ahead of new risks once identified and assessed.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This regime is well established and highly regarded internationally.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: But the landscape does not stay static and new risks emerge regularly.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Rather than to expect perfection at any point in time, our approach has been to stay responsive and to get ahead of the curve once these risks are identified and assessed.

sections.label: INTERPOL illicit proceeds estimate
sections.summary: INTERPOL states around US$2 to $3 trillion of illicit proceeds flow through the global financial system yearly.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: According to the International Criminal Police Organisation (INTERPOL), around US$2 to $3 trillion of illicit proceeds are channelled through the global financial system every year.

sections.label: Hong Kong money laundering arrests
sections.summary: In February, Hong Kong authorities arrested seven residents suspected of laundering US$1.8 billion from India online scams and illegal electronics and rare gems sales.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In February this year, the Hong Kong authorities arrested seven Hong Kong residents suspected of laundering US$1.8 billion of proceeds from online scams in India and the illegal sale of electronics and rare gems.

sections.label: Bill's three AML/CFT aims
sections.summary: The Bill seeks to align the AML/CFT framework with FATF standards, enhance detection and enforcement, and clarify processes for seized or restrained properties.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Bill seeks to: first, align our framework for Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism, or AML/CFT, framework with the FATF standards to better prevent and detect money laundering; second, enhance the ability of Government agencies to detect and enforce against money laundering through enhanced data sharing and strengthened prosecutorial levers; and third, clarify and improve our processes to deal with seized or restrained properties linked to suspected criminal activities.

sections.label: Lower CDD threshold
sections.summary: The CDD threshold will be lowered to cover single cash transactions or deposits involving $4,000 or more.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The threshold for CDD checks will be lowered from the current threshold of single cash transactions involving $10,000 or more or deposits into a deposit account involving $5,000 or more to cover single cash transactions or deposits involving $4,000 or more.

sections.label: IRAS and Customs data sharing
sections.summary: The amendments will let IRAS and Singapore Customs share tax data and trade data with Singapore's Financial Intelligence Unit.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The amendments will allow the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) and Singapore Customs to share tax data and trade data respectively, with Singapore's Financial Intelligence Unit.

sections.label: Prosecuting money laundering offences
sections.summary: Clause 11 amends section 56 of the CDSA so the prosecution need not prove laundered monies were criminal benefits or show the complete trail.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: To enhance our abilities to effectively prosecute money laundering offences, clause 11 of the Bill amends section 56 of the CDSA such that the prosecution will no longer need to prove that the monies allegedly laundered in Singapore were benefits from criminal conduct nor show the complete trail.

sections.label: Foreign environmental crimes as predicate offences
sections.summary: Clause 13 adds a Third Schedule designating illegal logging, land clearing, mining, waste trafficking and wildlife trade as money laundering predicate offences.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Clause 13 therefore introduces a Third Schedule to the CDSA, which will designate serious foreign environmental crimes as money laundering predicate offences.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We have taken a risk-based approach, aligned with FATF's recommendations, and propose to designate specific foreign environmental crimes which have been assessed to pose a higher risk of their proceeds being laundered in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: These are illegal logging, land clearing, mining, waste trafficking and wildlife trade.

sections.label: Court-ordered sale of seized property
sections.summary: Clauses 14 to 16 let the Court order sale of seized or restrained property without all parties' consent on depreciation, cost or justice grounds.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Clauses 14 to 16 will amend the CPC and the CDSA to allow the Court to order the sale of a seized or restrained property without the consent of all parties involved, provided the Court is satisfied that, the value of the property is likely to depreciate or undue costs are involved in maintaining the property; or the sale would be in the interests of justice.

sections.label: No disposal during absconded person investigation
sections.summary: Clause 16 amends the CPC so the Court must not dispose of seized property while investigation of a reasonably suspected absconded person is pending.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Clause 16 amends the CPC such that the Court must not dispose of the seized property, if there is any pending investigation in relation to an absconded person who is reasonably suspected of having committed an offence in respect of the property, regardless of the progress of the investigation.

sections.label: Absconded persons must present themselves
sections.summary: Clauses 16 and 17 require an absconded suspect of an arrestable or serious offence to present himself before a law enforcement officer before claiming seized property.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Clauses 16 and 17 amend sections 370 and 372 of the CPC, to include a requirement that an absconded person who is suspected of having committed an arrestable offence under our laws or serious offence under the CDSA, must personally present himself before a law enforcement officer to assist in the investigations, prior to making a claim to the property seized in respect of the offence.

sections.label: Depriving absconded suspects of gains
sections.summary: The amendments enable the Government to better deal with absconded suspects by depriving them of financial gains if they refuse to return to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Taken together, these amendments will enable the Government to better deal with absconded suspects, through depriving them of the financial gains of their money laundering and other criminal activities, if they refuse to return to Singapore for investigations.

sections.label: Tax and trade data sharing
sections.summary: The Bill's amendments will let Government agencies share tax and trade data with the Suspicious Transaction Reporting Office.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: First, the amendments in this Bill will empower Government agencies to share tax and trade data with Singapore's Financial Intelligence Unit, the Suspicious Transaction Reporting Office (STRO).

sections.label: Money laundering case storage expenses
sections.summary: Singapore's largest money laundering case, with $3 billion in seized assets, has incurred around $650,000 in storage, maintenance and safeguarding expenses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: The importance of these measures is underscored by Singapore's largest money laundering case to date, where the $3 billion in seized assets has already incurred around $650,000 in expenses for storage, maintenance and safeguarding.

sections.label: Four Bills and AML committee
sections.summary: Since 2023 four Bills have been passed, and an Inter-Ministerial Committee on AML expects findings and recommendations in fourth quarter of 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Since 2023, a total of four Bills have been passed in this House to safeguard our systems from exploitation and enhance our defences to protect the integrity of our systems.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: There is also an ongoing Inter-Ministerial Committee on AML, with findings and recommendations expected in fourth quarter of 2024.

sections.label: Business hub reputation and bank checks
sections.summary: Measures must not jeopardise Singapore's reputation as a competitive global business and finance hub, with feedback on protracted account opening and disproportionate checks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: However, Sir, we must ensure that these new measures do not come at the cost of jeopardising Singapore's reputation as a competitive global business and finance hub.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: I have received feedback and frustrations from affected parties that the account opening process is now protracted and delayed, with layers of checks perceived as disproportionate and not commensurate with the assessed level of risk.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Some have expressed concerns that our banks have taken a knee-jerk reaction in the reviewing accounts, issuing retroactive requests for documents and information that are cumbersome and time-consuming to produce, often seen as unnecessary given the accounts' sizes, tenure of the relationship with the financial institutions and transaction patterns.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Bankers fear their clients are bringing their money to other centres such as Switzerland, Hong Kong and Dubai.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Most businesses and investors are legitimate and checks must be risk-based, proportionate and considers the history of the relationship and transaction pattern.

sections.label: FATF mutual evaluation timing
sections.summary: FATF's most recent mutual evaluation of Singapore was in 2016, with the next one due next year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The most recent mutual evaluation by FATF on Singapore was done eight years ago in 2016, with the next one due next year.

sections.label: Recent $3 billion money laundering case
sections.summary: The recent $3 billion money laundering case is cited as an illustration.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To illustrate, we just need to look at the recent $3 billion money laundering case.

sections.label: Seized assets and victim restitution
sections.summary: Between January 2019 and June 2024, about $6 billion in assets were seized, with $416 million returned to victims.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the National Asset Recovery Strategy report, it was stated that in the five-and-a-half-year period between January 2019 and June 2024, authorities here seized about $6 billion in assets.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Out of this, the majority of $4.6 billion is still tied up in ongoing investigations and Court cases.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This leaves about $1.4 billion freed up to make restitution, out of which, $416 million, or less than one third, has been returned to victims.

sections.label: Judge on money laundering proof
sections.summary: The judge noted a person could be prosecuted for money laundering over monies mistakenly thought to be criminal proceeds but actually clean.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The judge noted that if the prosecution did not need to prove that the monies came from criminal conduct, then a person could be prosecuted for money laundering in situations where he mistakenly thought that the monies were the proceeds of crime when the monies were, in fact, clean monies.

sections.label: Suspicious transaction reports received by CAD
sections.summary: The Minister for Home Affairs revealed CAD received an average of 37,000 suspicious transaction reports yearly from 2019 to 2021.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In answer to a Parliamentary Question (PQ) I filed in January last year, the Minister for Home Affairs revealed that CAD received an average of 37,000 STRs each year from 2019 to 2021, or about 102 reports daily.

sections.label: DPT suspicious transaction reports
sections.summary: The Money Laundering National Risk Assessment report this year stated most suspicious transaction reports relating to DPTs did not point to any specific offence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to our Money Laundering National Risk Assessment report this year, a majority of the STRs relating to DPTs did not point to any specific offence.

sections.label: Workers' Party supports Bill
sections.summary: The Workers' Party is in support of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Workers' Party is in support of the Bill.

sections.label: Clause 11 money laundering knowledge
sections.summary: Clause 11 makes it sufficient for prosecution if the money launderer should reasonably know or believe he possessed criminal proceeds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Recognising the challenges, especially when crimes originate or when monies are dissipated through accounts overseas, clause 11 of the Bill makes it sufficient for prosecution if the money launderer should reasonably know or believe he possessed criminal proceeds, with no need to prove the complete trail of funds.

sections.label: Money laundering absconders
sections.summary: The passage notes that 17 remaining absconders come to mind in the $3-billion-dollar money laundering case.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: On the $3-billion-dollar money laundering case that the Minister had mentioned, the 17 remaining absconders come to mind.

sections.label: Cross-agency data sharing for financial intelligence
sections.summary: Clauses 18 to 21 let IRAS and Singapore Customs share tax and trade information with STRO to facilitate more holistic sense-making.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Next, I move to the enablement of cross-agency data sharing to enhance financial intelligence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This is pursuant to clauses 18 to 21, which allow IRAS and Singapore Customs to share tax and trade information respectively with STRO to facilitate more holistic sense-making.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I previously spoke in support of the Monetary Authority of Singapore's (MAS') Project COSMIC, or Collaborative Sharing of Money Laundering/Terrorism Financing Information and Cases, and I shared about the parable of the blind men and the elephant, and it is only by collecting information and thereafter pooling them all together, can a more accurate picture and understanding of money laundering risks emerge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I, therefore, welcome the amendment not only because it directly addresses a gap highlighted in Singapore's 2016 FATF evaluation, but more substantially, because it furthers an ecosystem approach to counter AML/CFT.

sections.label: Questions on STRO, COSMIC, seized properties
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister about STRO enhancing insights, integrating IRAS and Customs information with COSMIC, and absconder seized property cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Given the above, may I seek the Minister's view on (a) how may STRO further enhance the collection, pooling and delivery of insights to both the private and public sectors, to boost the effectiveness of entities' CDD, as the first lines of defence; and relatedly, secondly, whether information from agencies, such as IRAS and Customs, can be integrated with COSMIC that was launched in April 2024 this year, in the longer term, for more automated and secure sharing of intelligence across the entire financial ecosystem?

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Lastly, I spoke to and I note the amendments related to dealing with seized properties linked to suspects who have absconded, which introduce safeguards to prevent a premature release when investigations are ongoing to trace the absconder.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: On this, can the Minister clarify the prevalence of previous cases where an absconder had wilfully stalled investigations by staying overseas, and yet, successfully made a claim to seized properties?

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Was this observed with absconders in the $3 billion money laundering case, which continues to be of public interest?

sections.label: SFOs linked to money laundering convictions
sections.summary: In July 2024, DPM Gan Kim Yong revealed six SFOs with tax incentives were linked to individuals convicted in the money laundering case.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: In July 2024, Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong revealed that six SFOs awarded tax incentives were linked to individuals convicted in the recent money laundering case.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: The number of family offices in Singapore has grown by nearly 200%.

sections.label: MAS Public Consultation status
sections.summary: The passage asks for the current status of the MAS Public Consultation on Strengthening Defences Against Money Laundering Risk in SFOs.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: What, then, is the current status of the MAS Public Consultation on Strengthening Defences Against Money Laundering Risk in SFOs, launched on 31 July 2023?

sections.label: Licencing all SFOs
sections.summary: The passage suggests requiring all SFOs, regardless of tax incentive status, to register with and be licenced by MAS.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: To close the current regulatory gap, I suggest requiring all SFOs, regardless of tax incentive status, to register with and be licenced by MAS.

sections.label: illicit crypto wallets to conversion services
sections.summary: Chainalysis reports nearly $100 billion sent from known illicit wallets to conversion services since 2019, peaking at $30 billion in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: Chainalysis reports nearly $100 billion has been sent from known illicit wallets to conversion services since 2019, peaking at $30 billion in 2022.

sections.label: Jho Low associates art purchases
sections.summary: From May to September 2013, about $137 million from an account controlled by Jho Low's associates bought art at Christie's auctions.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: From May to September 2013, approximately $137 million from an account controlled by Jho Low's associates was used to purchase art at Christie's auctions.

sections.label: art-secured lending market growth
sections.summary: The art-secured lending market has expanded rapidly globally, with Sotheby's financial services originating over $10 billion in loans since inception.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: Globally, the art-secured lending market has expanded rapidly, with Sotheby's financial services alone originating more than $10 billion in loans since its inception.

sections.label: US Treasury art market AML report
sections.summary: The US Treasury recommended in a 2022 report that certain art market participants be subject to AML requirements including suspicious activity reporting and KYC.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: The US Treasury, recognising these risks, recommended in a 2022 report that certain art market participants be subject to AML requirements, including suspicious activity reporting and KYC requirements.

sections.label: whistle-blower fund from confiscated assets
sections.summary: The speaker proposes allocating a portion of assets confiscated from money launderers to establish a whistle-blowing fund.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: In our fight against money laundering, we must recognise the crucial role of whistle-blowers and create a system that incentivises proactive reporting and cooperation.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: I propose that we allocate a portion of the assets confiscated from money launderers to establish a whistle-blowing fund.

sections.label: whistle-blower award and fund provisions
sections.summary: Provisions include guaranteed awards of 10% to 30% of fines, a $300 million financial integrity fund, and expanded eligibility for non-US citizens and compliance professionals.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: Key provisions include: first, guaranteed awards of 10% to 30% of the financial fines collected for qualified whistle-blowers; second, establishment of a $300 million financial integrity fund funded by criminal forfeitures, fines and victim restitution; and third, expansion of eligibility to include non-US citizens, corporate auditors and compliance professionals.

sections.label: Singapore $3 billion money laundering case
sections.summary: The $3 billion money laundering case indicates a culture of viewing self-reported checks as administrative hurdles to be avoided for profits.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: For us in Singapore, the $3 billion money laundering case has indicated that there is somewhat of a culture of viewing self-reported checks as administrative hurdles to be avoided in the pursuit of profits.

sections.label: Whistle-blower fund from Fujian launderers
sections.summary: A whistle-blower fund seeded from the ill-gotten gains of the Fujian money launderers could be the cornerstone of a cleaner, more transparent financial future for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: A whistle-blower fund, seeded from the ill-gotten gains of the Fujian money launderers, could be the cornerstone of a cleaner, more transparent financial future for Singapore.

sections.label: Casino due diligence threshold reduction
sections.summary: Reducing the casino customer due diligence transaction threshold from S$10,000 to S$4,000 raises questions about its effect on small business owners and patrons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For instance, the reduction of the transaction threshold for customer due diligence checks in casinos, from S$10,000 to S$4,000, raises questions about its effect on small business owners and patrons who rely on these establishments for legitimate recreational or business purposes.

sections.label: Cost-benefit analysis for smaller enterprises
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Ministry conducted a cost-benefit analysis on operational feasibility and financial burden these measures may impose on smaller enterprises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Has the Ministry conducted a cost-benefit analysis on the operational feasibility and financial burden these measures may impose on smaller enterprises?

sections.label: Measures for coordination and jurisdictional conflicts
sections.summary: The question asks what measures are in place to ensure seamless coordination and avoid potential jurisdictional conflicts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: What measures are in place to ensure seamless coordination and avoid potential jurisdictional conflicts?

sections.label: Comparative analysis of FATF recommendations
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Ministry can provide a comparative analysis highlighting why certain FATF recommendations were adopted while others were not.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry provide a comparative analysis highlighting why certain FATF recommendations were adopted while others were not?

sections.label: $3 billion money laundering case
sections.summary: The $3 billion money laundering case negatively spotlighted Singapore, and MHA said amendments prevent premature release of seized properties during investigations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The recent infamous $3 billion money laundering case has cast a negative spotlight on Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: In MHA's press release of 2 July 2024, it was stated at paragraph 16 that, I quote, "...taken together, these amendments will prevent the premature release of seized properties while investigations are ongoing and avoid a situation where an absconded person evades investigations by staying out of Singapore and makes a successful claim to the seized properties because investigations have not been able to proceed".

sections.label: Lessons on AML due diligence
sections.summary: The MP asks what lessons the Government learnt about adequacy of AML due diligence by banks, property agents, precious stones sellers, lawyers and others.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Will the Government share with this House what are the lessons learnt from this case, if any, in respect of the adequacy of the current AML due diligence efforts required of the banks, property agents, sellers of precious stones or metals, lawyers and other service providers involved?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding the clarifications I seek, I support this Bill.

sections.label: Singaporeans shocked by laundering scale
sections.summary: Over the past year, many Singaporeans were shocked by the scale of the $3 billion money laundering scandal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Over the past year, many Singaporeans have been shocked by the scale of the $3 billion money laundering scandal.

sections.label: Tightening legal and sentencing framework
sections.summary: The speaker supports tightening the legal and sentencing framework and clause 11 removing the need to show a direct link under the CDSA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It is vital that we take steps to protect our reputation by tightening our legal and sentencing framework to deter money laundering.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We support the Government's decision to reduce the standard of proof for money laundering offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Under clause 11 of the Bill, the prosecution will no longer need to show under the CDSA the direct link between the criminal conduct and the monies allegedly laundered in Singapore.

sections.label: Short jail terms questioned
sections.summary: The Minister said imprisonment risk deters money laundering, but the 13 to 17 month jail terms appear short given CDSA provides up to three to 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In his written reply to my PQ on 8 May 2024, the Minister for Home Affairs told me that the risk of imprisonment is an important deterrent against money laundering.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, to an ordinary Singaporean, the jail terms of 13 to 17 months meted out to the nine men and one woman involved in the $3 billion money laundering case appear to be relatively short, especially given that the CDSA provides for jail terms of up to three to 10 years, depending on the nature of the money laundering offences.

sections.label: Actions against banks and corporates
sections.summary: The MP asks the Minister what actions were taken against each bank and corporate involved and what internal actions they took to strengthen AML regimes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Can the Minister tell us for each of the banks and corporates involved in this case, the actions that have been taken against them and the internal actions these institutions have taken so far to strengthen their AML Regime?

sections.label: Money laundering sentencing and PSP support
sections.summary: PSP asks why the 10 money laundering offenders got 13 to 17 months, seeks clarification on maximum penalty, and supports the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Many Singaporeans feel that the 13 to 17 months of imprisonment meted out to the 10 individuals involved in the $3 billion money laundering case is not sufficient to deter and prevent money laundering in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We would like to ask, under the existing CDSA, whereby money launderers can be sentenced to 3 to 10 years of imprisonment, why the offenders in the $3 billion money laundering case were only sentenced to 13 to 17 months?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Furthermore, we hope the Minister can clarify, under what circumstances that money launderers can be sentenced to the maximum penalty?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: PSP believes that in order to prevent money laundering and uphold Singapore's reputation and moral values in our society, we should increase the sentencing of money launderers and take strong measures against the implicated financial institutions. : PSP supports the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This Bill seeks to send a strong signal to the international community that Singapore is fully committed to combating money laundering.

sections.label: Regtech innovation and SME compliance costs
sections.summary: Enhanced compliance can spur regtech innovation but stringent AML/CTF measures can be financially burdensome, especially for SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Furthermore, the need for enhanced compliance can spur innovation in Regulatory Technology or regtech, leading to the development of new solutions to help businesses comply with the regulations more efficiently, positioning Singapore as a leader in the regtech innovation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, despite many favourable outcomes for the overall economy, this Bill could lead to certain challenges for businesses especially SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Implementing stringent AML/CTF measures often requires significant investments in technology, staff training, and process changes, which can be financially burdensome.

sections.label: Scope of new AML/CTF regulations
sections.summary: The passage asks which businesses and sub-sectors are directly affected by the new AML/CTF regulations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, regarding the scope and application of this Bill, could you please specify which businesses and sub-sectors are directly affected by the new AML/CTF regulations?

sections.label: Amendments on tracing, sale, claims
sections.summary: The speech focuses on amendments to remove overseas tracing, allow early sale of seized assets, and tighten third-party claims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: My speech is focused on the amendments: firstly, to remove the requirement to trace back the assets or proceeds as benefits of criminal conduct overseas; secondly, the early sale of seized assets; and lastly, tightening the criteria for third parties to claim assets linked to absconded persons still under investigations.

sections.label: Welcoming removal of tracing requirement
sections.summary: The passage welcomes the amendments to remove the requirement to trace back assets or proceeds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: As such, I welcome the amendments to remove this requirement.

sections.label: Welcoming early sale of seized properties
sections.summary: The passage welcomes the amendment to allow for the early sale of seized properties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Next, I welcome the amendment to allow for the early sale of seized properties.

sections.label: Early sale of assets
sections.summary: Early sale requires that the asset may depreciate or maintenance costs arise and that sale is in the interests of justice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Fourthly, the prerequisite to such early sale is that the asset may depreciate in value or undue costs will be involved in the maintaining of the property and that the sale will be in the interests of justice.

sections.label: Third party ownership claims
sections.summary: Amendments to the CPC tighten criteria for third party ownership claims over assets linked to absconded persons, aligning with common law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Usually, the perpetrators not only mask their illicit activities and transactions through layering of transfers and transactions but also through putting such assets in the names of proxies like family members or friends.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Hence, I welcome the amendments to the CPC to tighten the criteria of any ownership claims by third parties over assets linked to absconded persons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The amendments bring the position in line with the common law principle in AB Partners Pte Ltd v PP.

sections.label: Forfeited assets for community
sections.summary: A portion of forfeited assets could be set aside to benefit the community under criteria, as under section 298 of the Australian Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Perhaps, we can set aside a portion of such forfeited assets to be put up to benefit the larger community by establishing some criteria or guidelines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Under section 298 of the Australian Act, confiscated proceeds of crime can be reinvested in programmes for relevant purposes, including crime prevention and law enforcement.

sections.label: Bill amends other Acts
sections.summary: The Bill amends several other Acts and aligns with Financial Action Task Force recommendations.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Bill seeks to amend several other Acts and aligns with the recommendations of the Financial Action Task Force.

sections.label: Prosecution proof of knowledge
sections.summary: The prosecution need only prove the money launderer knew or had reasonable grounds to believe they dealt with criminal proceeds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: While I stand in support of the Bill, I have a few clarifications for the Minister.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: It would be sufficient for the prosecution to prove beyond a reasonable doubt that the money launderer knew or had reasonable grounds to believe that they were dealing with criminal proceeds.

sections.label: Data misuse and foreign crimes
sections.summary: The passage asks about guidelines and oversight for data misuse and how authorities will manage foreign environmental crimes as predicate offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will the Ministry share what kind of guidelines and oversight mechanisms have been established to prevent data misuse and ensure accountability?

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I urge the Ministries involved to implement robust data encryption and access control measures. : The prosecution will no longer be required to show a direct link between the money which had entered Singapore and the associated foreign crimes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Next, about the proposed change to designate serious foreign environmental crimes as money laundering predicate offences, how will the authorities manage the increased workload and complexity arising from the inclusion of foreign environmental crimes like illegal logging?

sections.label: Reputation, jobs, money laundering defences
sections.summary: Singapore's reputation affects job creation, and these amendments with four other Bills since May 2023 enhance defences against money laundering.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Singapore's reputation has an immense impact on job creation and securing good jobs for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: These amendments, along with four other Bills passed since May 2023, collectively enhances our defences against money laundering.

sections.label: Police powers and overreach guardrails
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister what specific powers the Police have under clause 16 and what guardrails prevent potential overreach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Their concerns about potential overreach should be addressed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Therefore, I would like to ask the Minister, what specific powers do the Police have under clause 16.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: What are guardrails are in place to prevent a potential overreach?

sections.label: Compliance burden from amendments
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister to ensure the amendments do not lead to an excessive compliance burden.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Could the Minister ensure that these amendments do not lead to an excessive compliance burden?

sections.label: Casino CDD threshold and seized assets
sections.summary: The Bill lowers the casino CDD threshold to $4,000, compared with the PSPM Act's $20,000, and Minister Shanmugam updated that the Police incurred about $646,282 as of March 2024 for seized assets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Just as an illustration, I note that the Bill is lowering the monetary threshold for casinos to perform CDD measures when it is entering into a single transaction of $4,000 or more with a patron.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: By way of comparison, the Precious Stones and Precious Metals (Prevention of Money Laundering, Terrorism Financing and Proliferation Financing) Act 2019 (PSPM Act), sets the threshold amount at $20,000 for a dealer of precious stones and metals to perform CDD measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: When I asked a PQ back in May 2024, Minister Shanmugam updated that the Police had incurred about $646,282 as of March 2024 for the storage, maintenance and safeguarding of the seized assets.

sections.label: Court order of sale powers
sections.summary: New powers let the Police or Public Prosecutor apply to Court for an order of sale if property is likely to depreciate, keeping it is dangerous, costly or not practicable, or sale is in the interests of justice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The new powers will allow the Police or the Public Prosecutor to apply to Court for an order of sale if the property is likely to depreciate in value, if keeping or maintaining the property would be dangerous, unduly costly or not reasonably practicable or if the sale would be in the interests of justice.

sections.label: COSMIC implementation and financial sector impact
sections.summary: The speaker asks for updates on COSMIC's phased implementation, its extension to non-financial gatekeepers, lessons learnt, MHA and MAS assessment of the laws' impact on financial flows, and engagement with compliance departments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: While I understand that MAS is taking a phased approach in the implementation of the COSMIC platform, starting with six major commercial banks, is there an update on when we would consider if it can be extended for use by a larger audience, including other non-financial institution gatekeepers, such as law firms and accounting firms?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: What is the status of the implementation of COSMIC and what are some of the lessons learnt so far?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Can MHA and MAS share their assessment of these new laws impact on the financial sector flows either directly or indirectly?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Would it be possible for the relevant agencies to engage the financial sector's compliance departments, to clarify that the efforts are targeted and aimed solely on illegitimate investments and should not be taken as a further broad tightening on all investment flows?

sections.label: CDSA section 56 amendment
sections.summary: Amended section 56 of the CDSA removes the need for the prosecution to prove property is benefits of drug dealing and criminal conduct.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Under the amended section 56 of the CDSA, the prosecution will no longer need to prove, as a physical element of the offences that property dealt with by the defendant is, in fact, the benefits of drug dealing and criminal conduct.

sections.label: STRO powers to obtain data
sections.summary: The proposed Bill gives STRO powers to obtain personal tax and trade data from several Government agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Under the proposed Bill, STRO has powers to obtain information on personal tax and trade data from a number of Government agencies.

sections.label: CDSA section 45 disclosure
sections.summary: Amended section 45 of the CDSA allows STRO officers to disclose information disclosed by a regulated person to a regulator.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The amended section 45 of the CDSA, allows STRO officers to disclose information disclosed by a regulated person to a regulator.

sections.label: CPC section 35 sale order
sections.summary: Amended section 35 of the CPC allows the court to order the sale of any seized or restrained property.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The amended section 35 of the CPC allows the court to order the sale of any property that is seized or restrained.

sections.label: Environmental offences in CDSA Schedule
sections.summary: The Third Schedule to the CDSA recognises environmental offences such as illegal mining, logging and wildlife trade as serious offences in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Third Schedule to the CDSA recognises environmental offences, such as illegal mining, illegal logging and illegal wildlife trade, as serious offences in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I welcome the Ministry's designation of illegal wildlife trade as a "foreign serious environmental offence".

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As a possible next step, I would again propose classifying certain wildlife crimes as serious offences in the Schedule of the Organised Crime Act.

sections.label: Classifying wildlife crimes question
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Minister can look into classifying wildlife crimes as serious offences in the Organised Crime Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Given this, can the Minister look into taking this next step to classify wildlife crimes as serious offences in the Organised Crime Act?

sections.label: Strengthening financial system after money laundering
sections.summary: Against the backdrop of the recent $3 billion money laundering case, decisive action is needed to further strengthen Singapore's financial system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Against backdrop of the recent $3 billion money laundering case, it is crucial that we take decisive action to further strengthen our financial system.

sections.label: Removing physical link proof requirement
sections.summary: The proposed amendments remove the requirement to prove a physical link, allowing prosecution based on the accused's intent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments remove this requirement to prove this physical link, allowing prosecution based on the intent of the accused.

sections.label: Foreign environmental crimes as predicate offenses
sections.summary: The Bill introduces a Third Schedule to the CDSA categorising serious foreign environmental crimes as predicate offenses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The Bill also introduces a Third Schedule to the CDSA, categorising serious foreign environmental crimes as predicate offenses.

sections.label: CDD checks for cash transactions
sections.summary: Under the new provisions, operators must conduct CDD checks for cash transactions or deposits of $4,000 or more, considering proliferation financing risks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Under the new provisions, operators must conduct CDD checks for cash transactions or deposits of $4,000 or more, considering the risks of proliferation financing.

sections.label: Singapore's Global Financial Centre Index ranking
sections.summary: Singapore was ranked third in the Global Financial Centre Index last year, behind only New York and London in competitiveness.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Singapore was ranked third in the Global Financial Centre Index last year, behind only New York and London in terms of competitiveness.

sections.label: Singapore's Basel AML Index ranking
sections.summary: The Basel AML Index of 2023 ranked 152 regions for money laundering risks, placing Singapore in the lowest quartile.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The Basel AML Index of 2023 ranked 152 regions around the world for money laundering risks.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Singapore was placed within the lowest quartile, which means that more than 75% of the regions presented higher AML risks than Singapore, and they include Hong Kong and Japan.

sections.label: National Asset Recovery Strategy launch
sections.summary: Singapore launched a National Asset Recovery Strategy and convened an Inter-Ministerial Committee to review its AML regime, with findings due in the fourth quarter.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We also launched our inaugural National Asset Recovery Strategy, which sets out Singapore's comprehensive approach towards the recovery of illicit assets from criminals for forfeiture and restitution to victims.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We convened an Inter-Ministerial Committee, or IMC, to review our AML regime, which will publish its findings in the fourth quarter of this year.

sections.label: No new financial sector requirements
sections.summary: The Bill introduces no additional regulatory requirements in the financial and real estate sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To be clear, this Bill does not introduce any additional regulatory requirements in the financial and real estate sectors.

sections.label: FATF casino CDD thresholds
sections.summary: FATF sets a lower CDD threshold of about S$4,000 for casinos than about S$20,000 for precious stones and metals dealers, based on assessed money laundering risks.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: FATF stipulates a lower CDD threshold of about S$4,000 for casinos compared to about S$20,000 for dealers in precious stones and metals based on the money laundering risks it has assessed for each sector.

sections.label: STRs filed in money laundering case
sections.summary: Financial institutions and other companies did file STRs for the recent money laundering case.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To Mr Tan's question on whether STRs were filed for the recent money laundering case, financial institutions and other companies had, indeed, filed STRs.

sections.label: Prescribed regulators get access
sections.summary: After the Bill is passed, other prescribed regulators such as ACRA and CEA will also have such access.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: After the Bill is passed, other prescribed regulators, such as ACRA and CEA, will also have such access.

sections.label: STRO data analytics system
sections.summary: In February 2022, STRO commissioned an enhanced data analytics and management system to process large volumes of STRs and other data into financial intelligence.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Like Mr Choo, Ms Foo and Assoc Prof Razwana, we recognise the need to leverage technology and optimise resources as we connect the dots in the sea of financial information.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: I shared previously that in February 2022, STRO commissioned an enhanced data analytics and management system to strengthen its ability to process large volumes of STRs and other data to be translated into richer financial intelligence.

sections.label: Money laundering amendment questions
sections.summary: Members asked about elements of proof, victim restitution and international cooperation, and the amendment allows better action against money laundering cases and persons exploiting the financial system.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Mr Choo, Mr Goh, Mr Leong, Ms Lim, Mr Ng, Assoc Prof Razwana, Mr Saktiandi, Mr Sharael Taha, Mr Wee and Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim asked about the elements of proof, impact on victim restitution and international cooperation.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This amendment will allow us to better act against money laundering cases and to pursue persons who exploit our financial system, whether the subject is a money mule or kingpin.

sections.label: MLA requests received
sections.summary: Singapore received MLA requests from 53 foreign jurisdictions in 2022 and 56 foreign jurisdictions in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To Ms Lim’s question, Singapore received MLA requests from 53 foreign jurisdictions in 2022 and 56 foreign jurisdictions in 2023.

sections.label: Third Schedule environmental crimes
sections.summary: A Third Schedule to the CDSA will let law enforcement investigate money laundering offences arising from foreign serious environmental crimes, which they previously could not do.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The introduction of a Third Schedule to the CDSA will allow law enforcement agencies to investigate money laundering offences arising from foreign serious environmental crimes, which they were previously not able to do.

sections.label: Police seized asset maintenance costs
sections.summary: The Police incurred over $600,000 in the last financial year to maintain seized assets in the recent case.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: As Ms Foo, Mr Saktiandi and Mr Zhulkarnain have pointed out, the Police have incurred over $600,000 in the last financial year, to maintain the seized assets in the recent case.

sections.label: Seized assets forfeited
sections.summary: Of the $3 billion in seized assets, $944 million have been forfeited and are being converted and appropriated into the consolidated fund.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Of the $3 billion in seized assets, $944 million have been forfeited and are in the process of being converted and appropriated into the consolidated fund.

sections.label: Seizure thresholds and disposal procedure
sections.summary: The proposed amendments do not change existing thresholds for seizure of properties under the CPC and concern the procedure for disposal of seized property.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To be clear, the proposed amendments do not change our existing thresholds for the seizure of properties, as expressly provided under the CPC – they concern the procedure for the disposal of seized property.

sections.label: Absconded persons money laundering case
sections.summary: Investigations are ongoing and none of the absconded persons in the recent money laundering case have returned to Singapore so far.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: As to whether this has been observed with the absconded persons in the recent money laundering case, investigations are still ongoing and I can only say that none of them have returned to Singapore so far.

sections.label: Penalties limited to jurisdiction
sections.summary: Penalties for convicted subjects can only cover offences committed in Singapore's jurisdiction, not offences committed outside it.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The penalties meted out to convicted subjects can only be for the offences committed in our jurisdiction and not for the offences they may have committed outside of our jurisdiction.

sections.label: Wildlife crimes under Organised Crime Act
sections.summary: The Government is studying Mr Ng's suggestion to prescribe wildlife crimes as a serious offence under the Organised Crime Act and will respond separately.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Mr Ng has suggested that wildlife crimes will be prescribed as a serious offence under the Organised Crime Act.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The Government is studying his suggestion carefully and will respond on this matter separately.

sections.label: Omnibus Bill for AML
sections.summary: On Ms He's suggestion of an Omnibus Bill for AML, it may be ideal but there is a trade-off between tidiness and timeliness.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: On Ms He's suggestion of an Omnibus Bill for AML, it may be ideal but there is a trade-off between tidiness and timeliness.

sections.label: Suspicious transaction reports effectiveness
sections.summary: The Government is not overly seized by a single number, but gatekeepers and sector regulators need to improve how they look at transactions and identify suspicious ones.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If you look at 20% of a very large number of STRs, are we happier that filers have chosen to surface information that they are concerned about and then we manage to find that only 20% of them are useful, or are we happier that they are very sparse with their filing and then the base becomes very small, but those that you can act on may be very high, and are you better off under those circumstances?

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I would say that we are not overly seized by a single number, but the point that the Member made is still a relevant one, which is that gatekeepers and their sector regulators need to improve the way in which they are looking at transactions and their effectiveness in identifying those that are suspicious.

sections.label: Sentencing regime comparable to jurisdictions
sections.summary: The sentencing regime is quite comparable to other leading jurisdictions.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: To reiterate, the sentencing regime is quite comparable to other leading jurisdictions.
